title: URL slugs for blog posts
blurb: A short warm-up: turn post titles into clean URL slugs and keep them unique when two posts share a title.
brief: You have a small blogging app. text.js already works, including a words() helper that splits a title into clean lowercase words, so no regex is needed. Finish slugify in slug.js so a post title becomes a URL slug, then write uniqueSlug in unique.js so a new post never reuses a slug that is already taken. The visible test file (a read-only tab) shows the expected behavior; some of its tests fail right now. A few extra edge cases you cannot see run when you finish.
requirements: text.js works: words(s) returns the words in s, lowercased with accents removed, so words("Hello,  Wörld!") is ["hello", "world"]. Leave it alone.
slugify(title, maxLength = 60) joins the words of the title with "-". So "Hello,  World!" is "hello-world".
The slug is at most maxLength characters. If cutting it leaves a "-" at the end, drop that too.
If there are no words (for example the title is "!!!"), the slug is "untitled".
slugify throws TypeError if title is not a string.

uniqueSlug(title, existing) returns slugify(title) if it is not in the existing array of slugs. Otherwise it tries base-2, base-3, and so on, and returns the first one that is not taken. It must not modify existing.
